problem: Semi-supervised instruction-following methods such as the Speaker-Follower train the speaker (trajectory→language) only on the small paired set, so unpaired trajectories never improve the speaker. Existing multimodal VAEs compress variable-length sequences into a single latent vector, which rules out the attention that seq2seq followers and speakers rely on.
motivation: Neural instruction followers need large amounts of paired trajectory–language data, e.g. hundreds of thousands of pairs even in the BabyAI gridworld. Unpaired trajectories are cheap to collect. A multimodal generative model with a shared latent can learn from unpaired trajectories by reconstructing them through that latent. The same model can then act as both follower and speaker, and the speaker can feed back into Speaker-Follower augmentation.
key_idea: Model trajectories and instructions with a multimodal sequential VAE (MS-VAE). Its shared latent is a fixed-length sequence of K vectors, extracted by learned-query 'bottleneck attention', so both modalities align in length and decoders can still attend to the latent. Train it on paired ELBOs plus a trajectory-only ELBO and a sliced-Wasserstein regularizer, then use it as a follower and/or as a better speaker for Speaker-Follower augmentation.
insight:
Bottleneck attention keeps nearly all the benefit of standard attention in fully supervised BabyAI. On BossLevel it reaches 87.1 SR with K=16, versus 89.6 for standard attention and 49.5 without attention; larger K helps on complex instructions (82.3 at K=4). The Table 2 ablations (M=1000 paired, N=1M unpaired) show three things:
- The unpaired-trajectory ELBO V drives the follower gain (SR 51.0→68.3 on GoToSeqLocal, 42.0→69.2 on BossLocal).
- MS-VAE on paired data only is actually worse than the supervised seq2seq baseline (51.0 vs 55.0 on GoToSeqLocal, 42.0 vs 45.8 on BossLocal).
- The domain-distance regularizer fixes the speaker overfitting that V causes: BLEU 10.86→11.73 on GoToSeqLocal and 5.97→7.42 on BossLocal, with SR also improving to 71.7 and 76.7.
The resulting speaker is complementary to Speaker-Follower augmentation: R2R val-unseen SR rises from 35.5 to 39.7.
method: Generative formulation: p(z,y,a|o)=p(z)p(y|z)p(a|z,o), where z is a shared task latent. Both the action decoder and the language decoder are autoregressive. The follower encodes z with q(z|y) (mean used at test) and decodes actions; the speaker encodes with q(z|a,o) and decodes language.

Mixture-of-experts posterior q(z|y,a,o)=½q(z|y)+½q(z|a,o), following MMVAE. The paired data use a tractable lower bound on the ELBO: per-modality reconstruction + cross-modal conversion − β·KL (β-VAE with β<1 to avoid posterior collapse). The prior is autoregressive (GRU, as in PlaNet).
Unpaired-trajectory objective V: a trajectory-only ELBO (reconstruct actions through q(z|a,o)) with weight γ, so trajectory-only data train the trajectory encoder and the action decoder.

Bottleneck attention: K learned token queries attend over the encoder hidden states (keys/values) to output mean/variance for K latent vectors z_1..z_K of dimension D. K is shared across modalities; decoders then attend over z instead of h. Settings: K=4 or 16 with D=128 on BabyAI; K=10 with D=512 on R2R.

Domain distance regularization: a sliced Wasserstein distance (50 projections) between the paired and unpaired trajectory-embedding distributions, computed per latent slot on the posterior means and summed. It is weighted by α and prevents the speaker from overfitting to action-only reconstruction.

Integration with Speaker-Follower: MS-VAE-follower uses the model directly as the policy. MS-VAE-speaker-follower uses the MS-VAE speaker to label the 178k unpaired R2R trajectories and train the follower, optionally with pragmatic inference (speaker-rescored beam search).

Initialization: MS-VAE is initialized from the trained baseline follower/speaker (Speaker-Follower LSTM architecture on R2R; BabyAI 1.1 architecture on BabyAI) and fine-tuned with the bottleneck module added.

setting.backbone: LSTM attention seq2seq follower/speaker from Speaker-Follower (R2R) or BabyAI 1.1 conv+LSTM follower and GRU encoder + 2-layer transformer-decoder speaker (BabyAI), plus bottleneck attention; trained, no pretrained LM
setting.training_data: R2R: R2R train pairs (paper cites 7189 annotated trajectories) + 178,000 unpaired trajectories from Speaker-Follower augmentation. BabyAI: M=1000 paired + N=1M unpaired trajectories for the semi-supervised experiments; M=1M paired for the architecture comparison.
setting.observation: R2R: panoramic RGB image features (same as Speaker-Follower). BabyAI: partial egocentric symbolic grid view.
setting.action_space: R2R: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (Speaker-Follower panoramic action space). BabyAI: discrete gridworld actions.
setting.privileged: none at inference. R2R follower early stopping (model selection) uses val-unseen SR; BabyAI reports the max smoothed SR over epochs.

numbers_note: R2R reports only NE/SR/OSR, with no SPL or TL. The greedy Speaker-Follower baseline has no test number ('-'). BabyAI SR is the max of per-epoch SR smoothed with a window of 5. R2R runs are single seed; the R2R follower was early-stopped on val-unseen SR.
results: On R2R, the MS-VAE speaker used for Speaker-Follower augmentation raises greedy val-unseen SR from 35.5 to 39.7 (test SR 37.9). With pragmatic inference, val-unseen SR goes from 54.6 to 56.9 and test SR from 53.5 to 56.1. The greedy result is comparable to Huang et al. (39.1), Yu et al. (38.9) and Fu et al. (38.8 val-unseen) but far below EnvDrop (52.2 val-unseen / 51.5 test). On BabyAI BossLocal with only 1000 paired demos, MS-VAE-follower reaches 76.7 SR versus 45.3 for the paired-only follower and 75.6 for Speaker-Follower. MS-VAE-speaker-follower reaches 82.6.
limitations: Absolute R2R performance is well below RL-based EnvDrop; R2R results are single-seed, and model selection uses val-unseen SR.
Only unpaired trajectories are exploited; using unpaired language is left to future work. Hyperparameters (α, γ, β, K) are set heuristically and are sensitive, e.g. β=1 causes posterior collapse.
The ablations run only on the authors' own miniaturized BabyAI tasks; the method is based on older LSTM seq2seq architectures, with no pretrained transformers.
